title: Rakesh Kumar v. State of U.P. & Ors.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
disposition: Writ dismissed for non-prosecution; interim discharged.
headnote: Writ challenging recovery of a remaining revised provisional assessment without decision of the consumer's objections, alleged to violate the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, dismissed for non-prosecution when none appeared for the petitioner. Any interim order stood discharged. No adjudication of the assessment or the Supply Code.
facts: Rakesh Kumar challenged recovery of Rs. 3,95,241 remaining under a Revised Provisional Assessment dated 18 October 2012, made after he deposited compounding fee. He filed objections on 1 November 2012. Without deciding them, respondent no. 5 by letter dated 9 November 2012 directed recovery of that amount. He alleged violation of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. On 3 December 2012 the Court granted time for a counter-affidavit and listed the writ. On 4 February 2016 none appeared for him.

holding_units.holding: The writ was dismissed for non-prosecution after none appeared for the petitioner on the revised list; any interim order stood discharged. The Court did not decide whether recovery of the remaining revised provisional assessment without deciding objections violated the Supply Code.

not_decided.point: Whether recovery of the remaining revised provisional assessment without deciding the consumer's objections violated the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005
not_decided.note: Writ dismissed for non-prosecution; no merits adjudication.
